title: Finite torsion open-unit test for norm-topological coefficients on regular affine limits
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its norm topology, and an algebraic closure $\Omega\supset E$ with its extended norm topology. Let $I$ be a small directed poset with least element $0$, and let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of regular affine finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume every transition $X_j\to X_i$ for $i\leq j$ is finite locally free, meaning affine with a locally finite free coordinate module [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For $f_0\in\Gamma(X_0,\mathcal O_{X_0})$ let $f_i$ be its pullback, assume each $f_i$ is a nonzerodivisor, and put $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$, $W=X[1/f_0]$ and $j:W\hookrightarrow X$. The affine limit is the spectrum of the filtered colimit of the coordinate rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-affine-spectrum].
Use small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each $s\geq1$ let $A_{s,X}$ be the constant sheaf of $\mathbf Z/\ell^s\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Suppose that the actual derived open unit
$$A_{s,X}[0]\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*A_{s,X}[0]$$
is an isomorphism for every $s\geq1$ in the ordinary uncompleted derived module category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $F=E$ or $\Omega$ put $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$, using all continuous maps for every profinite set $P$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and $C_{F,Z}=p_Z^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules, ordinary unbounded derived categories and K-injective total derived direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Then for every affine pro-etale $v:X'\to X$, every finite-rank lisse $C_{F,X'}$-module $N$ (pro-etale locally finite free [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]), and $j':W\times_X X'\hookrightarrow X'$, the actual unit
$$N[0]\longrightarrow Rj'_*j'^*N[0]$$
is an isomorphism. The identity open, empty schemes and rank zero are allowed. No completeness of $\Omega$, no finite-coefficient-field descent of $N$, and no replacement of $C(-,\Omega)$ by a union of finite-field function sheaves is assumed.

Bhatt--Scholze Section 6.8 treats complete finite fields; HRS Lemma 7.9 uses the colimit topology and is not this assertion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-torsion-open-test-devissage] to the given affine limit $X$, its principal open $W$, and the stipulated cyclic derived units. For every affine weakly contractible $V\to X$, with $T=V\times_XW$, this gives the actual restriction isomorphism for every constant abelian group killed by a power of $\ell$, including infinite groups, and the degree-zero bijection for $\mathbf Z/\ell$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned torsion-acyclic norm-coefficient test, proof steps 1-3: derived unit on affine weakly contractible tests, exact finite-primary devissage, then arbitrary bounded torsion by filtered continuity.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-complete-norm-open-test] to each pair $V,T$ from step 1. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization](1), $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is the localization $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/V$ and $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ that at $T$, so sheaves on $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ over $h_V$; an epimorphism onto the terminal sheaf of $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is an epimorphism onto $h_V$ in $\mathrm{Sh}(X_{\mathrm{proet}})$, hence splits, so the terminal object of $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is weakly contractible, and the restriction isomorphisms of step 1 are the hypothesis of that node. The conclusion gives the actual scalar restriction isomorphism for every complete nonarchimedean normed extension $B/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with the specified quotient and rationalization maps.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned torsion-acyclic norm-coefficient test, proof steps 4-5: unit-ball quotient construction for complete B, epimorphic derived limit, and rationalization by multiplication by ell.

proof.text: The tower, nonzerodivisors and fields satisfy exactly the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-norm-scalar-test-assembly]. Step 1 supplies its cyclic degree-zero bijection and step 2 its complete-field tests. Thus $R\Gamma(V,C_{F,V}[0])\to R\Gamma(T,C_{F,T}[0])$ is the actual restriction isomorphism for both $F=E,\Omega$ and every affine weakly contractible $V\to X$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned torsion-acyclic norm-coefficient test, proof steps 6-7: clopens and component spaces in degree zero; complete E and positive-cohomology injection into the norm completion of Omega.

proof.text: For each $F=E,\Omega$, apply [lem-sfb-lisse-open-unit-test-descent] with $\Lambda=C_F$ and the scalar tests of step 3. It gives the actual unit $N[0]\to Rj'_*j'^*N[0]$ for every affine pro-etale $X'\to X$ and every supplied lisse $C_{F,X'}$-module $N$, exactly as asserted. Its statement includes rank zero, empty schemes and identity opens.

The assembly proof is 1450 characters. No node restates the item or one of its clauses, and there is no cycle or SGA use. Each node is true. N1: the slice unit gives RΓ(V)→RΓ(T); finite ℓ-torsion induction and filtered continuity then cover infinite M, which N2 needs because O_n is infinite for B=C_ℓ. N2: ℓ^nO is a neighbourhood basis, completeness gives O=lim O_n, Milnor with epimorphic transitions applies, and C_B=colim(L,·ℓ) since functions on qcqs |U| are bounded. N3 matches lem-sfb-norm-completion-positive-cohomology-mono hypothesis for hypothesis: E is complete, Ω̂ is complete, and degree 0 comes from the clopen/π_0 comparison. N4 works for arbitrary Λ: weakly contractible objects of (U_i)_proet stay weakly contractible in X_proet, and sections-conservative(2) applies. Edge cases checked: f a unit, f=0, T empty with V nonempty (the hypothesis then fails), rank 0, B=Q_ℓ and B=C_ℓ. The duplicate search with rg -L over open-unit, contractible, clopen and unit-ball patterns found no existing statement of any new node.
